close_reason: Fixed: renamed NcTypeMask::contains() to intersects() at definition and all 5 call sites.
description:
pkix-path/src/lib.rs:1151–1153

The method is:

    fn contains(self, other: NcTypeMask) -> bool { self.0 & other.0 != 0 }

'contains' conventionally means 'all bits of other are set in self' (i.e. self & other == other, a subset test).  What this actually computes is 'at least one bit of other is set in self' — that is the standard meaning of intersects() from the bitflags crate and from std's Flags trait.

Using the wrong name will mislead a reviewer:
- nc_constrained_types.contains(NC_TYPE_RFC822) reads as 'RFC822 is fully contained in the mask' — which is accidentally correct for single-bit masks but breaks down the moment someone passes a multi-bit mask.
- The bitflags crate convention (intersects vs contains) is well-established in the Rust ecosystem.

Fix: rename to intersects() and update all call sites (seven occurrences).
title: NcTypeMask::contains() should be named intersects()
